races.name: Dragonbet Welsh Racing Festival 9th-11th Oct Nursery Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Courseyoudo
runners_data.note: Hold-up profile from trainer Tom Lacey who has a modest 14-day strike rate (1/4); 60 days off the track is a significant query, and all recent form comes on Good ground with no soft-ground evidence — watch the market for any support given the absence.

runners_data.name: Crystal Kraken
runners_data.note: Rossa Ryan is a key booking for Dylan Cunha's yard (6/26 in 14 days shows trainer in form); two recent runner-up finishes at 5f on Good ground show this horse is consistent and prominent-racing, making it the most natural challenger to Our Fella from just off the pace.

runners_data.name: Our Fella
runners_data.note: The confirmed pace-setter for this race; Ashley Lewis (3lb claim) keeps the weight competitive and the horse's recent form over 5f includes placings in nearly every outing — uniquely positioned to control tempo, though headgear (p) noted and soft ground is an unknown variable for this front-runner.

runners_data.name: Lion Of Persia
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer trained by Robert Cowell, who has solid juvenile sprint ability; three runs in, with a second most recently on Good ground at 5f — needs a strong pace to run into, which is not guaranteed here, and 47 days off adds a fitness question.

runners_data.name: Naval Cop
runners_data.note: Trained by Andrew Balding — yard in strong form (11/65 over 14 days) — but this is a genuine hold-up horse whose natural closing position is cramped in a six-runner field; Alfie Redman's 7lb claim helps the weights but the style-fit penalty (0.92) is material and its chance depends on conditions that may not materialise.

runners_data.name: Devon Angel
runners_data.note: Returned just two days ago (LR:2d) which is an immediate flag; soft-going record is one placing from six attempts, so the surface is a genuine concern — a natural hold-up type operating below its preferred conditions and without the scope to secure an ideal position in this small field.

races.paceDynamic: Our Fella is the sole confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, should be able to bowl along at a controlled, self-selected tempo from the gates on this straight 5f at Chepstow. The going is Good to Soft — softer than anything in Our Fella's recent history but the horse has form across a variety of Good ground races at 5f, and a sustainable gallop rather than a scorching early pace is the most likely outcome. Crystal Kraken is the most natural prominent horse capable of pressing from close off the pace, but the hold-up contingent — Courseyoudo, Lion Of Persia, Naval Cop and Devon Angel — will be tracking from midfield or further back. This field contains more hold-up types than the race map can accommodate at the rear: Naval Cop and Devon Angel are genuine closers repositioned to midfield in the mapping, but in a six-runner field on a straight course they are likely to end up further back than that suggests. The overall shape strongly favours a horse that can race prominently and travel into the race without burning fuel, making the prominent-to-lead profile the primary beneficiary of this predictable, single-pacemaker setup.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Our Fella Controls Wire-To-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Our Fella bowls into an uncontested lead and sets a sustainable pace that the soft ground keeps honest.
scenarios.body: Our Fella dictates from flag-fall, ticking along at a tempo that saps the closers' ability to accelerate on testing ground, reaching the line with enough left in the tank to repel any challenger. A 5f straight with no pace pressure and soft ground is the ideal platform for a confirmed front-runner to exploit.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Racer Reels In Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Our Fella goes slightly too hard early and Crystal Kraken, tracking just off the pace, collects in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Crystal Kraken's recent form shows consistent placing — twice second at 5f on Good ground — and Rossa Ryan will be alive to the opportunity to press from just off the pace if Our Fella overcooks it. The soft ground could blunt Our Fella's stamina enough to let the chasing Crystal Kraken sweep by.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Mow Down Field
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong and the soft ground creates a slow final furlong that suits horses finishing from the back.
scenarios.body: Lion Of Persia, who has shown the ability to finish strongly at 5f, would be the most credible beneficiary given natural hold-up tendencies and Good-to-Soft form in its most recent run. Courseyoudo has a closing profile but form figures have been modest and it hasn't been close enough at the business end to inspire confidence.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistributed Types Spring Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If Naval Cop or Devon Angel manage to secure a better position than their redistribution suggests and the pace collapse hands them a late opportunity.
scenarios.body: Both Naval Cop and Devon Angel are true hold-up horses squeezed into a small field, and Devon Angel arrives on just two days' rest with limited soft-ground form — significant negatives. Naval Cop carries better raw form credentials but the style-fit discount and amateur rider combination make this a long-shot scenario.

watchPoints.text: Our Fella's front-running role is unchallenged but watch if Ashley Lewis (3lb claimer) allows the fractions to quicken too sharply on soft ground — if the early splits are fast, the closers will have a rare opportunity to pounce.
Devon Angel ran just two days ago; if there is any visible sign of fatigue or reluctance at the stalls, downgrade its already-limited chance significantly in this soft-ground sprint.

Naval Cop's redistribution from true hold-up to mapped midfield masks the reality that in a six-runner straight 5f, it could end up further back than useful — watch how Alfie Redman positions it in the first furlong as a read on its live chance.

Crystal Kraken is 22 days fresh and Rossa Ryan is a high-quality booking; any market move for this horse pre-race is meaningful given its consistent placing profile and the prominent position it can naturally secure.

The going report lists 5f as Good to Soft throughout the card — softer than the Good ground on which most of these juveniles have built their form — so monitor the early going and any trainer/jockey comments, as ground conditions could compress the field's finishing spread.

races.name: Eddie & Sandra Hayward Supports Noahs Ark Charity Restricted Maiden Stakes (For Horses In Band D) (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Anna Belardo
runners_data.note: Sole front-runner with Dr Newland & Insole sending her back out after 102 days off; her three-run form shows she handles Good and has finished in front before, and she gets a soft lead here which is the crucial tactical advantage in this shape.

runners_data.name: Beechwood Glory
runners_data.note: John Butler's filly has placed twice over this course and trip on Good, and her T14 return of 1/16 suggests the yard is ticking over; her natural style is hold-up, and she will be operating at the back of this small field, meaning she needs the pace to be genuinely honest to get competitive.

runners_data.name: Conscientious
runners_data.note: Single-run record of ninth on Tapeta at Southwell tells us very little for a turf debut on Good to Soft; the fade-in-finish flag is a significant caution on a track where resolution through the final furlong is non-negotiable, and Archie Watson's 2/20 T14 strike rate offers modest confidence.

runners_data.name: Ischgl
runners_data.note: Rossa Ryan takes over for Ciaran Murphy's consistent filly who has placed twice on soft and twice on Good over this exact trip; the sim-going record of 0 wins from 2 placed runs on soft is honest rather than spectacular, but the proximity to the pace suits her best in this race shape.

runners_data.name: Texas Crown
runners_data.note: William Carson partners this Daisy Hitchins-trained filly who has finished second twice on Firm — a very different surface to today's Good to Soft — and her one Good-ground run ended eleventh, making this ground test a notable unknown that tempers optimism.

runners_data.name: Washington Royale
runners_data.note: Michael Appleby's consistent sort has three runs on Good all resulting in fourth or fifth, suggesting a horse who gets into the race but struggles to find a decisive finishing effort; Pat Dobbs is an experienced booking and a prominent pitch suits, though the ceiling looks limited based on form.

runners_data.name: Foxsbrush
runners_data.note: John Ryan's lightweight (128lbs) runner has finished tenth and seventh on Good ground over today's distance and trip, and with a hold-up style she needs significant improvement on those bare figures just to be competitive; the T14 figure of 2/6 is the one modest positive.

races.paceDynamic: Anna Belardo is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with only three prominent types (Ischgl, Texas Crown, Washington Royale) likely to press rather than lead, she should be able to dictate from the front without being seriously harassed into a suicidal pace. On Good to Soft ground over Chepstow's flat 6f, a controlled leader who can set her own rhythm and avoid being pressed ragged is in a powerful tactical position, and Anna Belardo fits that profile precisely. Beechwood Glory and Conscientious are genuine hold-up types who will be racing towards the rear regardless of how the map plots them, meaning the closing kick they need must come from genuine ground-eating late runs, which is harder to manufacture when the pace is merely sustainable rather than scorching. This race shape strongly favours a prominent-to-front-running profile that can control the tempo, conserve energy through the middle, and repel challengers over the final two furlongs — Anna Belardo and whichever prominent type tracks her most efficiently are the chief beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Leader Controls, Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Anna Belardo breaks cleanly, establishes an uncontested lead, and the prominent trio track without forcing her into an unsustainable gallop.
scenarios.body: Anna Belardo dictates a measured pace on the Good to Soft ground, conserves energy through the middle portion, and simply has too much in hand for rivals forced to make up ground late; Ischgl and Washington Royale, closest in pursuit from a prominent pitch, are best placed of those who try to reel her in.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Closer Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent trio apply enough early pressure to force Anna Belardo into a slightly elevated gallop that she cannot sustain to the line.
scenarios.body: A fractionally-above-comfortable pace drains Anna Belardo in the final furlong, and the horse who tracked most efficiently in second or third — Ischgl, given her soft-ground placed form and course experience — produces a timely challenge; Washington Royale's consistency at this trip makes her the next most likely beneficiary of a weakening leader.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Storms Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to string the field out and set up a meaningful closing burst from the rear.
scenarios.body: Beechwood Glory, whose hold-up style suits a race where the front end has burned itself out, produces a sustained late run down the centre; Conscientious, despite the fade-in-finish flag, could also pick up late scraps if the pace is genuinely honest, though the form book offers little encouragement.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Messy Break, Wide Open
scenarios.trigger: If there is significant trouble at the start, a false break, or an early collision that disrupts the anticipated race shape entirely.
scenarios.body: With the race order scrambled, horses revert to opportunistic tactics and the form book becomes less relevant; any of the prominent types who manage to find a clean run from chaos could benefit, but this is a low-probability scenario in a small, well-behaved field.

watchPoints.text: Anna Belardo's draw and early speed will be critical — watch whether she breaks cleanly and secures the lead unopposed, because any stumble or slow start hands the race shape to the prominent types immediately.

Ischgl is the most likely pressure point on Anna Belardo; if Rossa Ryan sends her forward early to sit a close second rather than a tracking third, the gallop could lift enough to compromise the leader's stamina late on Good to Soft ground.

Beechwood Glory and Conscientious are both genuine closers in a field where the pace could be quite modest — if Anna Belardo goes very steady, their finishing kicks may arrive too late over only 6f to catch a rested leader.

Texas Crown's two placed runs came on Firm ground and her Good-ground form is poor — monitor her market move; any significant support would suggest connections have intelligence about her handling of today's going that the form book does not yet show.

Foxsbrush carries the lightest weight in the field at 128lbs; in a soft-ground maiden where the race could get grindy late, even a modest ability edge can be partially offset by that weight relief, so do not dismiss her entirely if the market shortens her up.

races.name: Paving Fields Construction Restricted Maiden Stakes (For Horses In Bands B, C And D) (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Lucky Radar
runners_data.note: Lightly raced with no recent form shown, Rod Millman's runner arrives with an unknown style but a high OR of 120 suggesting significant ability; going is unknown so soft ground is a genuine uncertainty, and Edward Greatrex takes the ride for a yard capable of placing horses well first or second time out.

runners_data.name: Flag Of Nations
runners_data.note: William Muir and Chris Grassick send this OR=120 runner out with a similarly blank form slate, and Lewis Edmunds keeps the ride simple with no style data to anchor a read; the soft ground is an open question, but the rating band implies this runner should be competitive if fit and handling conditions.

runners_data.name: Perola
runners_data.note: Richard Hughes's runner has raced prominently before and will lead here, giving her a clear positional edge in this contest, though her OR=71 and mixed recent form — including a 5th on Good — means the drop in class is needed to win; the 91-day break is worth noting, and the STYLE_FIT tag suggests her chance is marginally tempered by being asked to lead when that may not be her optimum role.

runners_data.name: Persian Gate
runners_data.note: Archie Watson's runner showed a respectable fifth on Tapeta last time and returns 15 days later with Rossa Ryan, a high-profile booking that commands respect; a hold-up horse by profile, the soft ground presents no flagged concern and a straight six at Chepstow gives a true closing run if the pace is adequate.

runners_data.name: Geemann
runners_data.note: Joe Tickle's gelding carries a modest sim-going record of 0 wins and 0 places from 8 efforts in similar conditions, and its recent form string — featuring a 10th and 11th — makes the current task look very demanding; naturally a hold-up type, the competitive race shape means it is unlikely to get as far back as it prefers, and the STYLE_FIT discount applies here given its redistribution into midfield on the map.

runners_data.name: Kodicall
runners_data.note: J S Moore's runner finished second on Firm last time and has shown enough consistency across three runs — including a second — to be taken seriously; a hold-up horse on Good or Firm ground, the switch to soft is a mild concern worth monitoring, and William Cox will need the pace to be genuine to deliver this one's finish from off the back.

races.paceDynamic: Perola is the sole confirmed front-runner in this six-runner maiden and will stride into the lead from the off, setting what should be a measured, uncontested gallop on Good to Soft ground over Chepstow's straight six. With no genuine rival willing to challenge for the lead, Perola controls tempo entirely, meaning the pace is unlikely to be truly searching — a scenario that historically compresses the field rather than blows it apart. Persian Gate, Geemann and Kodicall are all hold-up types by nature, meaning late closers will need a strong enough gallop to enable a winning run from off the pace, and that is not guaranteed when one horse dictates alone at a comfortable tempo. This race shape — a lone, uncontested leader setting a sustainable clip — strongly favours horses with tactical speed and the ability to press or track from a prominent or mid-division position, making sit-and-sprint hold-up profiles risky unless the pace is genuinely hot.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Perola Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Perola leads throughout at a comfortable tempo and the soft ground blunts any late surge.
scenarios.body: Perola dictates from the front with no pressure, setting fractions that suit a thorough stayer-ish type on testing ground and keeping finishes tight enough to reward the leader and any horse that travels close behind; Persian Gate, with a single run to its name and clearly placed for this, has the profile to track and challenge if fit and forward enough.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If a lightly raced unexposed runner holds a prominent pitch and outstays Perola in the closing stages.
scenarios.body: Lucky Radar or Flag Of Nations, both unknown entities with unraced-style profiles, could hold a close tracking position and produce a decisive late burst that the soft ground amplifies; their lightly raced status and higher official ratings suggest connections expect them to be competitive and they may carry natural tactical speed that puts them in the perfect spot.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Reel Them In
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves genuinely fast enough to soften the front two and allow the hold-up horses to finish powerfully.
scenarios.body: Should Perola's solo lead string the field out faster than anticipated, Kodicall and Geemann could emerge from behind with a sustained late run, as both have shown ability to close on quicker ground; however, Geemann's redistribution from its natural rear position means it may not get far enough back to produce a true closing run, limiting the credibility of this shape.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Soft Ground Lottery
scenarios.trigger: If the testing conditions cause widespread stopping and produce an untidy race won by the best traveller on the day.
scenarios.body: An unexpectedly gruelling surface turns this into a stamina test rather than a speed contest, randomising the result and potentially bringing the hold-up horses into play as leaders tire sharply; this is a low-probability shape in a maiden over six furlongs where only one horse has confirmed soft-ground credentials.

watchPoints.text: Watch Perola's early gallop — if she settles into an uncontested crawl through the first two furlongs, hold-up horses like Persian Gate and Kodicall will be severely disadvantaged as the race becomes a sprint from the front.

Persian Gate's jockey booking of Rossa Ryan is notable for a horse with just one run on an artificial surface — watch the market for any significant move that would signal confidence in a significant fitness or ability update.

Lucky Radar and Flag Of Nations are both OR=120 maiden runners with unknown styles and no going data; if either drifts badly in the market it may signal connections are unconvinced about soft ground or readiness, which would meaningfully reshape the probabilities.

Geemann's soft-ground record (0 wins, 0 places from 8 similar-going runs) is a concrete red flag — if conditions are confirmed testing rather than just good to soft, its chance of featuring meaningfully in any scenario is further reduced.

Monitor whether Perola shows any signs of reluctance or greenness at the start after a 91-day absence — any slow break would immediately hand the initiative to the tracking runners and open the race up considerably.

races.name: Runtech Ltd Handicap Stakes (Div I)

runners_data.name: Prince Ali
runners_data.note: An 8yo handicapper in good-to-soft sim-going form (1W1P from 15 runs) who has won over 8f on soft, but a true hold-up type pushed into a midfield slot here because of the crowded rear — his chance hinges on finding a clean path through in a congested field.|

runners_data.name: Escape Magic
runners_data.note: The race-shaper: a 3yo who has won consecutive 7f starts on good ground for Owen Burrows, gets a straightforward lead here with Rossa Ryan aboard, and the soft ground is within their compass — this is the horse everyone else has to account for.|

runners_data.name: Fullstop
runners_data.note: Grace Harris's 3yo has shown modest but consistent form at 7f on good ground, is suited by a soft surface per sim-going (2 places from 9), wears a hood and has the 3lb claim of Ashley Lewis to help — a genuine midfield hold-up type racing in her natural position here.|

runners_data.name: Ashford Hill
runners_data.note: A 5yo who is a natural hold-up horse shuffled into midfield on the map; sim-going returns are modest (0W0P from 15) and trainer Dominic Ffrench Davis has had a quiet 14-day strike rate — needs everything to go right in a messy race to feature.|

runners_data.name: Blue Point Express
runners_data.note: A 4yo for Adrian Wintle who wears a hood and has some good-ground placing (1W2P from 15 sim-going runs), but is another genuine closer compelled to race closer to the pace than ideal — the 62-day absence and modest recent form (95-054) are further reasons for caution.|

runners_data.name: Pacific Prince
runners_data.note: Flags exist for this 5yo: a tendency to fade in the finish is noted alongside a dire recent form string (-0060B) and 83 days off — James Bennett's runner is running out of role in midfield and faces a stiff task on any reading.|

runners_data.name: Aplaceinthesun
runners_data.note: Ollie Sangster's 3yo carries a "fades in finish" flag and recent form (08-740) is unencouraging; a natural closer being asked to race further forward than ideal here, and on soft ground over 7f the fade tendency could be amplified.|

runners_data.name: Snow Day
runners_data.note: Tony Carroll sends out this 3yo who also carries a fade flag; form (0-0866) reflects a horse that has struggled to land a blow in handicap company, and being forced into midfield rather than a natural hold-up position does not help a profile that lacks the late burst needed at this trip on soft.|

runners_data.name: Margorie
runners_data.note: Eve Johnson Houghton's 4yo has won on soft ground and placed there too (1W1P from 10 sim-going runs), wears a hood and is weighted at the top of the field (135lbs) — a genuine midfield type with soft-going credentials who could creep into contention if Escape Magic weakens.|

runners_data.name: Nammos
runners_data.note: John & Rhys Flint's 6yo has been placed on fast ground over further but has never won at this sim-going level; 19 days since last run is positive and Mason Paetel's 3lb claim helps, though a history of placing at 8f suggests the 7f on soft is the key stamina question.|

runners_data.name: Ajrad
runners_data.note: Rod Millman's 8yo has a decent sim-going record (1W1P from 15 runs) and wears a hood, but is a natural hold-up type repositioned into midfield — 13 days since last run is a positive flag and Lewis Edmunds' experience at this level means the horse could find a better position than the map implies if others drift back.|

races.paceDynamic: Escape Magic is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 11-runner 7f handicap on good-to-soft ground at Chepstow, and with no genuine rival to press them from the gates, Rossa Ryan can dictate an unhurried, sustainable gallop throughout. The soft-ish surface will stretch the field out early and reward stamina over raw speed, meaning any pace set by Escape Magic is unlikely to be suicidal — rather a controlled, metronomic tempo that keeps the door ajar for closers only if they can travel smoothly. The field is loaded with true hold-up horses — Ajrad, Prince Ali, Aplaceinthesun, Blue Point Express, Pacific Prince, Ashford Hill and Snow Day are all natural closers who have been redistributed into midfield on the map because there is simply no room for all of them to drop out at the rear in reality; of these, Ajrad and Prince Ali, both carrying headgear and with decent recent form, are best placed to secure a forward-enough midfield berth. This race shape firmly favours horses that can sit just off the pace in third or fourth, travel within themselves, and quicken over the final two furlongs — in other words, Escape Magic if they get an easy lead, or any horse nimble enough to track them closely from a handy position without burning fuel early.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Escape Magic Dictates Alone
scenarios.trigger: If Escape Magic is allowed to stride into an uncontested lead and control the tempo throughout on the soft ground.
scenarios.body: Rossa Ryan settles Escape Magic into an unchallenged rhythm, the pace proves just moderate enough on soft ground that the leader retains plenty in reserve entering the final two furlongs, and a horse with three wins in four runs over this trip has the class to hold on. Horses who travel prominently and switch off quickly — Nammos and Margorie, both proven on soft/good-to-soft — are best positioned to capitalise if Escape Magic does tie up.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Handy Tracker Swoops
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is just steady enough that a horse sitting second or third can conserve energy and pick off Escape Magic in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Nammos and Margorie, both mapped genuinely in midfield and with soft-ground form, track the leader without burning reserves on the climb home and produce the late punch the scenario demands. Nammos in particular has placed at 1m on faster ground and shortening to 7f on soft could sharpen their finish, making them the prime profile here.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Storms Late
scenarios.trigger: If early congestion and a traffic-heavy midfield forces a genuine come-from-behind run, and the pace collapses in the final 100 yards.
scenarios.body: With so many redistributed hold-up types crammed into midfield, a messy race could see gaps appear late and a true closer get a clear run to mow down a tiring leader — Fullstop, with sim-going form and a 3lb claim for Ashley Lewis, is the most credible profile here. However, this scenario is structurally discounted because the majority of the field's "closers" are not true hold-up types and are unlikely to be positioned far enough back to generate genuine late momentum.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Collapse; Chaos Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Escape Magic is headed before halfway and the race breaks into a rough, error-strewn contest with no true pace-setter left standing.
scenarios.body: Without a dominant leader, the field fragments, sectionals become uneven, and the race degenerates into a sprint from three furlongs out that could throw up an unlikely winner — Snow Day or Aplaceinthesun, both running out of role but benefitting from positional luck, could profit. This is the least likely shape given Escape Magic's clear front-running credentials and Rossa Ryan's ability to control the race from the front.

watchPoints.text: Escape Magic (Rossa Ryan) — if allowed to stride clear unchallenged in the first two furlongs, a horse with back-to-back 7f wins could build an unassailable lead on softened ground before the closers can organise.

Midfield congestion — with seven horses redistributed from the rear into the midfield map zone, watch for early crowding and interference as genuine hold-up types resist their unnatural positions, creating traffic risks for Fullstop and Nammos in the final two furlongs.

Ajrad and Prince Ali (both in headgear) — if either manages to secure a tracking position closer to Escape Magic than the map suggests, their soft-ground profiles and recent form make them more dangerous than their official odds may reflect.

Nammos — running from a mark of 54 over a shorter trip than their recent 8f runs, the drop to 7f on soft ground is worth monitoring in running; if they travel kindly in second or third, the finishing effort could prove stronger than their modest sim-going record implies.

Pacific Prince (83 days off, fade flag, form -0060B) — a potential early-race casualty to monitor; if this runner shows signs of distress or is pulled up, it could cause interference for horses immediately behind in the midfield cluster.

races.name: Runtech Ltd Handicap Stakes (Div II)

runners_data.name: Marisitta
runners_data.note: Won last time out (OR 50, 6f, Good) under William Carson and clearly has current form, but her natural hold-up style means she is bumped forward into midfield in this slow-pace race shape — John O'Shea sends her out 13 days fresh and she has only one placing in 15 similar-going runs.|

runners_data.name: Eye Of The Water
runners_data.note: A 10-year-old who has shown consistent placing ability over 8f on soft and good-to-soft; Callum Hutchinson takes over after a 61-day break, which is a significant concern, but the horse travels prominently enough to benefit if Vape's pace is weak.|

runners_data.name: It's A Mugs Game
runners_data.note: Lightly raced 3-year-old from Joe Tickle's yard (0/4 in 14 days), whose three-run career shows only a fourth and a sixth at best — the step up from 6f to 7f is untested and the soft surface has already caught her out (10th at 6f soft).|

runners_data.name: Lady Margret
runners_data.note: Tony Carroll's yard has been busy (4/41 in 14 days) and the apprentice Myla Coppins takes a 5lb claim, but this mare has finished 6th, 8th, 10th, 10th, 12th in recent starts — her hold-up style is essentially redundant here as she will be pressed into midfield, which has never suited her.|

runners_data.name: A Rose Adaay
runners_data.note: Grace Harris's 4-year-old has placed consistently at 8f on good ground and the drop to 7f on soft may concentrate her effort; Ben Ffrench Davis claims 5lb which is useful, though she has run 12 times in similar going without a win — naturally inclined to come from behind but will be shuffled forward in this slowly-run race.|

runners_data.name: Lady V
runners_data.note: Unknown style (tagged U), lightly raced 3-year-old with 91 days off the track — Rossa Ryan is an upgrade in the saddle for Charlie Pike, but all three career runs have produced bottom-half finishes and there is no soft-ground form to draw on.|

runners_data.name: Big Moonrise
runners_data.note: David Evans has two winners in 17 runs over 14 days and Edward Greatrex takes the mount; this 3-year-old showed a third place over 7f on standard ground so the trip is not an issue, but his hold-up inclination will be squeezed forward by the race shape — soft ground is untested.|

runners_data.name: Kaiko
runners_data.note: Adrian Wintle's 3-year-old has managed only a fifth as best career finish across four runs, all on good or firm; Laura Coughlan claims 3lb but the horse has never handled soft ground and ran out of room at 8f — the hold-up style is wasted in this pace context and the scope for improvement looks limited.|

runners_data.name: Vape
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner and race-shaper: a 9-year-old at OR 55, top-weight at 135lbs, ridden by 7lb claimer Amy Tucker — Vape has placed on soft ground before and controls the tempo entirely, but all recent finishes have been in the bottom half of the field and the weight burden is real.|

runners_data.name: Rovinia
runners_data.note: Roger Teal's 4-year-old arrives in the best recent form in the race: 1st, 2nd, 2nd, 2nd in her last four outings, including a win over 7f on standard and places over 8f on good — Owen Lewis (5lb claim) is a positive booking, and if Rovinia can get into a comfortable rhythm from a midfield berth she looks the most consistent threat.|

runners_data.name: Angel's Call
runners_data.note: Nikki Evans sends out this 5-year-old 19 days after her last run having won over 8f on good going and placed twice in similar company; Ryan Kavanagh claims 3lb and she has good-to-soft form showing (2nd and 3rd in sim-going runs) — naturally a hold-up horse who will be pushed forward, but her recent winning profile gives her solid claims if she can find daylight.|

races.paceDynamic: Vape is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 11-runner field and will lead from the off at a sustainable, uncontested gallop over Chepstow's flat 7f on good to soft ground — no rival is likely to challenge for the lead, meaning Vape sets whatever tempo suits. With just one pace-setter, the early fractions figure to be moderate rather than scorching, which compresses the field and makes a true end-to-end stamina test less likely; instead, the race will likely quicken in the final two furlongs with position at the two-pole proving crucial. That dynamic strongly favours runners who can travel in a handy position through the early stages and produce a sustained finish, rather than deep closers who depend on a strong pace to power through from the rear. The field holds considerably more hold-up horses than the map can accommodate at the rear — Rovinia, Angel's Call, Marisitta, Lady Margret, A Rose Adaay, Big Moonrise and Kaiko are all natural hold-up types, but most will be pushed forward into midfield or prominent positions simply by the lack of early pace, with only the quickest to load and most flexible jockeys likely to secure their preferred spot.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Vape Controls, Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Vape leads uncontested and the pace remains moderate throughout, allowing the front-runner to dictate and the field to stall in a slow-run race.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Overhaul Late

scenarios.body: Rovinia is the standout case here, having finished 1st, 2nd, 2nd, 2nd in her last four starts and clearly going through a purple patch; Angel's Call also has recent winning form at OR 51 and can produce a sharp late effort.

scenarios.label: C

scenarios.body: Lady Margret or Big Moonrise, pushed wider and forward by the congested hold-up group, accidentally secures a prominent berth and sustains it on softish ground that blunts speed from behind; this is the least likely shape given the redistribution of so many true hold-up types.

watchPoints.text: Rovinia has won or placed in four consecutive starts and arrives as the form horse in the race — watch whether Owen Lewis can slot her into a prominent enough midfield position given the slow pace, as any delay in getting cover could cost her the race.|

races.paceDynamic: Revelance and Homeland are the two confirmed front-runners in a 17-runner field, and with both likely to want to lead, the opening half-mile on Good to Soft ground at Chepstow will see a genuine, contested pace rather than a false gallop. Revelance carries top weight of 138lbs for Ralph Beckett and Rossa Ryan and has recent winning form over the trip, making it the more likely pace-dictator, while Homeland (Zoe Lewis, 7lb claimer) will press and ensure the tempo is honest throughout. This field contains significantly more hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate at the rear — Moonhall Lass, Too Much Trevor, Redhot Whisper, Bobby Dassler, and Scarfo are all genuine hold-up horses redistributed into midfield slots because they are unlikely to find their natural position in a 17-runner handicap with a packed field; the prominent spots behind the two leaders are most likely to be secured by Thanos, Rating, Kodi Fire, and Eutropia. A contested, honest pace on softening ground over a mile at Chepstow strongly favours prominent racers who can track the speed, stay in a good position through the bends, and quicken in the straight — pure hold-up horses face the additional burden of negotiating traffic and cover in an unusually deep field.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Pace, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Revelance and Homeland fight for the lead setting a genuine gallop, the horse best placed just off them at halfway takes full advantage.
scenarios.body: The honest pace on Good to Soft ground drains the front two in the closing stages, and a prominent racer who has tracked in second or third position swoops in the Chepstow straight. Thanos and Kodi Fire both have the positional speed to sit just off the pace and the form to land a blow when the leaders tire.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If Revelance is allowed to control proceedings at a measured tempo, using Rossa Ryan's experience to manage the pace and conserve energy.
scenarios.body: Revelance's recent winning form over the course and distance, top-class handler in Beckett, and the advantage of dictating from the front could prove decisive if Homeland is unable to sustain the challenge past halfway. On Good to Soft, a horse that controls its own fractions without being harried into a truly punishing pace retains significant reserves for the straight.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Threads Through
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace burns exceptionally hot and creates a genuine closing opportunity for horses coming from off the pace in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Redhot Whisper has the most convincing hold-up profile with recent placed efforts over the mile on similar ground, and Nakaaha posted a win at the trip and has soft-ground form. However, several runners in this position are redistributed types not operating in their true role, which tempers the probability of a late-closing winner.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Grind, Stamina Wins
scenarios.trigger: If the combination of a big, competitive field and deepening Good to Soft ground produces an attritional gallop where stamina rather than tactical position becomes the overriding factor.
scenarios.body: Auburn Avenue and Spirit Of The Bay, both hold-up types with each-way profiles for the Flint yard that recorded a winner in the preceding 14 days, could stay on late if the race turns into a test of endurance. This remains the least likely scenario given the pace map and the redistributed nature of most hold-up runners.

watchPoints.text: Revelance and Homeland are on a collision course for the lead — if neither concedes and they fight it out under top weight on Good to Soft ground, both could be weakening inside the final two furlongs, opening the door for everything positioned just behind them.

Scarfo has the strongest sim-going placed record among the redistributed hold-up horses but will be squeezed into midfield in a 17-runner field — watch whether Isobelle Chalmers (7lb claimer) can find a clean passage before the final bend.

Grace Harris runs three horses (Rating, Too Much Trevor, Nakaaha) and team tactics could play a role — if Rating is ridden prominently to soften up the opposition, Too Much Trevor or Nakaaha could be the intended beneficiary in a yard with five wins from 20 in 14 days.

Thanos is 60 days off the track for Harry Charlton — the yard has been active (3/13 in 14 days) and the 3-year-old's upward form trajectory makes the return fitness angle the key watch point early in the race.|

Going reports across the card consistently read Good to Soft rather than the Soft declared for this race — if the ground is riding on the better side, the prominent and front-running styles gain an additional advantage over closers who prefer genuinely soft conditions.

races.paceDynamic: Control Room and Level Up are both confirmed front-runners and will contest the lead from the outset over this straight 5f at Chepstow, creating a genuinely contested early gallop rather than a dawdle. On Good To Soft ground that honest early pace will be sustained and the tempo is unlikely to relent, meaning horses that race prominently without having to burn energy fighting for position will be best placed. The field also contains more hold-up and prominent types than can comfortably fill every rear position — Some Nightmare is a true hold-up horse redistributed to the midfield on the map because the race shape simply won't produce the gap at the back they'd naturally seek. This contested lead scenario with soft ground underfoot decisively favours horses who can sit just off the pace in the slipstream, avoiding the front-running duel while still having early cover — prominent-to-midfield types with soft-ground form are the primary beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Lead, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Control Room and Level Up fight each other for the front and honest early sectionals on soft ground set up a race for the stalkers behind.
scenarios.body: The two front-runners burn each other off through the first couple of furlongs, leaving them vulnerable to a well-positioned prominent horse swooping from the slipstream in the final 1f; soft ground amplifies the toll of the early duel.

scenarios.label: B

scenarios.label: C

scenarios.body: An unusually hot early tempo produces a race where the whole field folds close together at the 2f pole, and horses with proven soft-ground stamina find the longest stride late; however, the true hold-up types face positional issues as the pace redistributes the field.

races.paceDynamic: Ghost Story is the sole confirmed pace-setter in this field and will be allowed to bowl along unchallenged at the head of affairs over 1m2f on soft ground at Chepstow, creating a controlled, sustainable tempo that is unlikely to be seriously contested. The remainder of the field — Meet Me In Meraki, Stipulation, Zambezi Magic, and Staywitherjohnny — are all genuine hold-up types redistibuted into midfield on the map, meaning the race will be strung out behind Ghost Story with a cluster of closers hunting it down in the straight. The field holds considerably more hold-up and come-from-behind types than the map can accommodate at the rear; Ghost Story is the only runner realistically capable of securing the front, with Liberate the most likely to track it from a genuine hold-up style despite being mapped further back. On soft ground over this trip with a lone, uncontested leader, a steady-to-moderate pace suits those capable of getting close enough to the leader through the race, as a genuine sustained sprint finish on this ground will be less decisive than track position — horses racing handy or able to make smooth headway from midfield are most advantaged.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Ghost Story Dictates Alone
scenarios.trigger: If Ghost Story is allowed to set a comfortable, uncontested lead and controls the tempo throughout without being pressed.
scenarios.body: Ghost Story bowls along on a line into the straight with a stack of true hold-up types struggling to peg it back on soft ground over a trip that rewards front-runners allowed their own way; the soft surface blunts the finishing kick of the closers and rewards the leader's stamina. Those who have tracked closest — potentially Liberate if it settles off the pace — are best placed to challenge, but the pace-setter retains a major advantage.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Grind Through
scenarios.trigger: If the soft ground genuinely tests stamina and the hold-up types produce sustained late runs to reel in Ghost Story inside the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Ghost Story's advantage is eroded as the soft ground increasingly favours those coming from off the pace with stamina reserves intact, and Meet Me In Meraki or Zambezi Magic — both proven in softer conditions — grind past in the closing stages. This scenario requires the closers to get into a striking position early enough, which their redistributed midfield placement makes slightly more achievable than if they were true backmarkers.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Mover Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If one of the redistributed hold-up types manages to secure a tracking position close enough to Ghost Story to challenge with a decisive turn of foot in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Stipulation or Meet Me In Meraki, running from a midfield berth rather than their natural deeper position, lands a blow if the pace slackens and they can quicken past a tiring leader; this is a lower-probability shape because these runners are out of their natural role and must race more prominently than they prefer. Soft ground and 1m2f suit the profile on paper, but style fit is discounted given each horse's redistribution flag.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Pair Clear Field
scenarios.trigger: If Ghost Story and one close tracker — most likely Liberate — press hard enough to drop the rest and fight out a two-horse finish.
scenarios.body: A moderately honest pace draws the field into a lung-testing contest on soft ground that decimates the hold-up types who cannot sustain their run, leaving only the handy-placed horses in contention; Liberate's solid recent form at shorter trips and hold-up style theoretically suits a late sprint if it gets close enough. This scenario is the least likely given how deep all challengers sit and the lack of any secondary pace-maker.

watchPoints.text: Ghost Story — watch whether it is allowed to bowl along unchallenged out of the gate; if anything briefly hassles it for the lead in the first furlong, it will have to work harder than expected and its advantage shrinks considerably.

Meet Me In Meraki and Stipulation — both are true hold-up horses racing closer than natural due to field congestion; watch whether they can settle in a tracking position or are forced wide and back, as either outcome significantly alters their winning chance.

Soft ground verification — the going report lists this race as Good To Soft across all returns, yet the pace dynamic notes Soft; if the ground is genuinely softer than posted, Ghost Story's stamina-based front-running style gains further weight and the closers' finishing kicks are blunted.

Staywitherjohnny — Rossa Ryan is an informative booking but watch the horse's early positioning; if it fails to travel smoothly in the first half-mile on unfamiliar soft ground it is unlikely to land a blow from the back of a small field.
